section: 4 Algebraic renormalization of SUSY gauge theories with constant ghosts
title: An anomalous breaking of supersymmetry in supersymmetric gauge theories with local coupling (+ companion: Calculating the anomalous supersymmetry breaking in super-Yang-Mills theories with local coupling)
journal: Nucl. Phys. B620 (2002) 55-83; companion Phys. Rev. D65 (2002) 105003
claim: When the SYM gauge coupling is promoted to an external real superfield G = (eta + eta-bar)^(-1/2) (local coupling), the Wess-Zumino-gauge ST identity with constant SUSY ghosts acquires a one-loop anomalous breaking: the BRS variation of a monomial containing ln g times the YM Lagrangian (eqs. (31)-(32)), coefficient r_eta^(1) = C(G)/(8 pi^2) (eq. (38)), which vanishes for constant coupling, is gauge and scheme independent, and cannot be removed by a local counterterm - only shifted between the ST identity and the eta - eta-bar identity, or absorbed into a coupling-dependent modification F(g^2) of the SUSY transformation of g^2 (eqs. (47)-(50), (61)-(62)). It generates the two-loop gauge beta function from one-loop data; the NSVZ form corresponds to the choice F = 1/(1 - r_eta g^2) (eqs. (65), (104)-(106)), which the paper says is not distinguished.
loop_order: anomaly first at 1 loop; consequences for beta at 2 loops and a closed all-order form depending on normalization
theory: N=1 SYM (plus axial vector and charged multiplets for multiplicative renormalizability, eqs. (7)-(10)), WZ gauge, local coupling
scheme: algebraic (quantum action principle); BPHZL and DREG with MS stated to satisfy the eta - eta-bar identity by construction (eq. (41)); companion paper computes the coefficient from convergent one-loop integrals (fermion triangle with axial-current insertion, bosonic graphs with topological-current insertion) in Feynman gauge with a background gauge, divergent parts fixed by transversality; agrees with a DREG computation by Bos (ref. [20] there); DRED not discussed
symmetry_argument: ST identity S(Gamma_cl) = 0 (eq. (26)) and eta - eta-bar identity (eq. (27)); anomaly coefficient scheme/gauge independence via BRS-varying gauge parameter (eqs. (51)-(52)) and RG argument (eqs. (53)-(57))

proved: existence and uniqueness (up to shifting) of the one-loop anomalous breaking of SUSY in WZ gauge with local coupling; non-removability by local counterterms (Sec. 3, 4)
two-loop beta function fixed by one-loop beta, r_eta^(1), the Adler-Bardeen coefficient r^(1) = -C(G)/(16 pi^2) (eq. (71)) and gamma^(1): eq. (104)
explicit one-loop value r_eta^(1) = C(G)/(8 pi^2) from convergent integrals (companion, Sec. 4, eqs. (27), (79), (80))
assumed: quantum action principle for the extended (local-coupling) ST identity
the NSVZ form is a normalization choice, not derived (paper's own statement)
checked_partially: companion: Feynman-gauge simplifications attributed to apparent accidental cancellations; gauge independence argued algebraically

evidence: hep-th/0107239: eq. (5) local coupling; (26)-(27) identities; (31)-(32) anomaly; (38) coefficient; (47)-(50) shifting; (61)-(62) modified SUSY transformation; (65), (104)-(106) beta function forms; (70)-(71) Adler-Bardeen anomaly
hep-ph/0110323: eqs. (24)-(27) beta relation; (41), (44)-(47), (60)-(68) Green functions and graphs; (73)-(80) result in Feynman gauge
red_flags: shows that a constant-ghost ST identity can carry a genuine (non-removable) anomaly once couplings are local external fields, although no SUSY anomaly exists at constant coupling - a BV treatment with background couplings must include it
the closed NSVZ-type formula is normalization dependent
cross_checks: relation to holomorphic vs canonical coupling (Arkani-Hamed-Murayama rescaling anomaly) mentioned as not apparent (hep-ph/0110323 Sec. 5)
source_access: full text via ar5iv (both papers; App. B of the first not reached); INSPIRE for journal data
notes: Lead corrected: the anomaly is not Pontryagin-like; it is the BRS variation of a ln g x Lagrangian monomial. Relevant to any BV/QME analysis with x-dependent couplings or with the coupling in front of the kinetic term.
